current_episode.title: What If We Maintained Fire Hydrants Like We Maintain Our Cars?

guest.bio_context: Paul started his engineering career at a valve and hydrant company in Elmira, New York, working in the foundry, product development, and quality. He has returned to the hydrant and valve industry after a circuitous career path, now based in Chattanooga, Tennessee at Mueller Water Products, where he identifies market opportunities and develops innovative solutions like the Hydrant Renewal program. His daughter also works as an engineer at Mueller Water Products.

context.real_quote: Never be satisfied with the way things are. There's always something better.

pending_qa.q: What is the average age of fire hydrants in municipal water distribution systems?
pending_qa.r: In a survey conducted at a trade show, utilities provided ages ranging from 10 years old to 40 or 50 years old. In a more detailed assessment, Paul Gifford walked home from work and recorded the age of 25 hydrants between his workplace and Highland Park, finding an average age of 50 years, with the newest installed about 5 years ago and the oldest dating to 1910.

pending_qa.q: What are the maintenance advantages of proactive hydrant renewal compared to reactive failure management?
pending_qa.r: Proactive maintenance, similar to automotive oil changes every 3,000 to 4,000 miles, can help water distribution systems work better, last longer, and create less risk of fire damage. All internal parts of fire hydrants are accessible from the ground by removing the top and using a wrench, and because hydrant parts have remained essentially the same design for 50 to 70 years, Mueller still manufactures compatible replacement parts that can restore hydrants to like-new or better-than-new condition with improved materials, pressure ratings, and flow.

pending_qa.q: How has Mueller Water Products invested in manufacturing capabilities over the past decade?
pending_qa.r: Mueller has invested heavily in three of its foundries over the last 10 years, with employees involved in those investments expressing enthusiasm about the company's future direction. The company operates a lost-foam foundry that represents state-of-the-art technology not currently used by competitors in the market space.

pending_qa.q: What advice does Paul Gifford offer to newcomers considering careers in traditional manufacturing industries?
pending_qa.r: While the fire hydrant, gate valve, and foundry industries may appear old and unexciting on the surface, the modern processes and automation technologies available are compelling. The lost-foam foundry technology is state-of-the-art, and experiencing the reality of molten iron, machinery, and modern manufacturing processes demonstrates that the industry is far more innovative and engaging than external perceptions suggest.
